places.name: Colosseo
places.description: The world's largest amphitheatre, built 72–80 AD. Held up to 80,000 spectators. Three-level tour includes hypogeum (underground animal and gladiator staging) and arena floor. A feat of Roman engineering still unmatched.
highlights: Hypogeum — underground gladiator staging area
Arena floor access (timed entry)
Night tours — floodlit travertine at sunset

places.name: Piazza Navona
places.description: Baroque Rome at its most theatrical: three fountains, including Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers (1651). Built on the footprint of Domitian's 1st-century stadium. Aperitivo terraces all around the oval perimeter.
highlights: Bernini's Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi (1651)
Footprint of Domitian's 86m stadium still visible
Evening aperitivo on the south terrace

places.name: Musei Vaticani
places.description: 54 galleries including the Raphael Rooms and Sistine Chapel (Michelangelo's ceiling and Last Judgment). Book 2–3 months ahead for peak season. Early morning tours before crowds arrive at the Sistine.
highlights: Sistine Chapel — Michelangelo's Creation of Adam
Gallery of Maps — 40 topographic frescoes (1581)
Raphael Rooms — four papal apartments

places.name: Campo de' Fiori
places.description: Morning market in a square where Giordano Bruno was burned in 1600. Local artichokes, Norcia truffles, Roman street food. Transforms into Rome's most raucous outdoor bar after dark.
highlights: Morning market for Roman artichokes
Norcia black truffles in season (winter)
Piazza turns into bar terraces after sunset

places.name: Pantheon
places.description: Built 126 AD by Hadrian, perfectly preserved. The oculus (9m open eye) is the only light source in the dome. Geometrically perfect: dome diameter equals floor-to-oculus height (43.3m). Raphael's tomb inside.
highlights: The oculus — 9m open hole, no glass
Perfect sphere: height equals diameter
Raphael's tomb and burial of Italian kings

places.name: Trastevere
places.description: Rome's medieval neighborhood of ochre-washed houses, ivy-covered lanes, and the oldest Christian basilica still in use. Santa Maria in Trastevere (12th c.), trattorias, cobblestones after 10pm.
highlights: Santa Maria in Trastevere — 5th-century mosaics
Best cacio e pepe at Da Enzo al 29
Cobblestone alleys closed to traffic after 8pm

places.name: Vittoriano — Altare della Patria
places.description: The monumental white marble 'typewriter' completed in 1935. Controversial at construction — six blocks of medieval Capitoline Hill were demolished. Elevator to the terrace for the best free panorama of Rome: from the Colosseum to the Vatican.
highlights: Free elevator to summit — 360° Rome panorama
Free admission to the monument itself
Eternal Flame of the Unknown Soldier

places.name: Tazza d'Oro
places.description: Rome's finest espresso at the steps of the Pantheon since 1946. House-roasted beans, standing-only bar, famous summer granita di caffè con panna. Never sit down — espresso in Rome is a standing art.
highlights: Espresso at the Pantheon steps — 1946 roaster
Granita di caffè con panna — summer ritual
Standing-only bar: 30 seconds, no table tax
